newsitem.title: USA: Dallas sets up sports authority for new arena.
newsitem.headline: Dallas sets up sports authority for new arena.

text.p: Dallas has set up a sports authority to help it build a new arena for the city's professional basketball and hockey franchises, officials said on Thursday.

City Manager John Ware said the city council met Wednesday evening and unanimously approved his request for the sports authority, which will be able to borrow money, condemn land and build a new arena.
"It gives us another tool to use in financing the development and construction of a new sports arena," Ware told Reuters, adding that there were several tax advantages to setting up such a body.

The National Basketball Association franchise Dallas Mavericks and National Hockey League team Dallas Stars have been involved in months of tortuous negotiations with city authorities aimed at building a new sports arena.
Ware said he expects a deal to be reached this fall.
The new sports authority should start work next week once the city council appoints its seven-member board. It will need approval from the city council to borrow money or condemn land.

It is not yet clear how much the city will contribute to building a new arena but officials are studying the possibility of applying a wide variety of new taxes, including a car rental tax, a hotel room tax, and taxes on parking and tickets at the sports events.
